verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between (-)-alpha-Amorphene and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, as the compound is linked through multiple pathways to this transporter. In Path 1, (-)-alpha-Amorphene is directly associated with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 2B1, which in turn is a target of a compound (methyl (1R,4S,5R,9S,10S,13R,15S)-15-acetyloxy-5,9-dimethyl-14-methylidenetetracyclo[11.2.1.01,10.04,9]hexadecane-5-carboxylate), which itself targets the 1B1 member. In Path 2, (-)-alpha-Amorphene is also linked to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 2B1, which is a target of Nystatin, a known inhibitor of the 1B1 transporter. Similarly, in Path 3, (-)-alpha-Amorphene is associated with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 2B1, which is a target of aminohippurate, another compound that interacts with the 1B1 transporter. These findings collectively suggest that (-)-alpha-Amorphene may act as a modulator or inhibitor of the 1B1 transporter, potentially through interactions with its substrates or inhibitors. The evidence is consistent across different pathways, indicating a plausible mechanism of action, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
